title: OptiMind Daily Log
description: Canonical schema for daily/YYYY-MM-DD.json — the structured per-day record holding today's protocol (the morning-brief-generated plan) plus the structured log (sleep/meals/caffeine/snacks/routine/metrics/workouts) captured from the dashboard. One file per day in optimind-journal, alongside journal/YYYY-MM-DD.md. Authoritative for numeric values; every field written here is mirrored to journal/<date>.md as a Dashboard-role line (see journal_entry.schema.md §Role write contract). Routine/protocol item ids use the snake_case form of the canonical grep keywords in journal_entry.schema.md (e.g. cold_shower, deep_work) — do not invent synonyms.

schema_version.description: Schema version. Bump via a migrations/daily_log_<from>to<to>.py script. 1.1 adds the optional `note` provenance field to log/protocol entries and the `status` enum to routine items; it is a pure relaxation, so every valid 1.0 document is a valid 1.1 document.

date.description: The user's LOCAL date (the configured timezone; America/New_York by default), matching the journal/<date>.md filename. Never a bare-UTC-derived date.

tz.description: IANA timezone the date and all HH:MM times are expressed in (e.g. America/New_York).

protocol.description: The plan for the day, regenerated each morning by the morning-brief Routine (§7.4). Absent until generated.

generated_at.description: When this protocol was generated. ISO-8601 with explicit offset; bare 'Z' is banned.

source.description: Provenance: default fallback, a mobile-chat override the user requested for today, or derived from user_profile rules + state.

log.description: Structured log captured during the day. All sub-fields optional — a day may be partially logged.

routine.description: Map of routine-item id (snake_case canonical keyword) → completion record.

metrics.description: Map of daily-metric id (snake_case) → a numeric reading tracked over days — e.g. mood, energy, soreness, hrv, resting_hr, weight_kg. For subjective/graded signals that are NOT routine completions (use `routine` for binary done/not-done items). The morning-brief and analyst read these for trend + rule gating (e.g. a rule that only fires once a tracked metric crosses a threshold).

LocalTime.description: 24-hour HH:MM local time in the file's tz.

TimeWindow.description: HH:MM-HH:MM local window, or a bare HH:MM for point-in-time items (a supplement dose, lights-out) that have an instant rather than a span. Both forms appear in the historical record.

Note.description: Free-text provenance for this entry — how the value was arrived at, not what it is. Written whenever a number is inferred rather than stated ("time estimated", "latte caffeine estimated"), or a completion carries a qualifier ("SKIPPED (user-stated)", "only L-Threonate taken"). Load-bearing: the Dashboard badges an estimated value differently from an observed one, and an entry that silently drops its note is indistinguishable from a measurement.

OffsetDateTime.description: ISO-8601 datetime that MUST carry an explicit numeric offset. Bare 'Z' (UTC) is rejected by the pattern, matching the timezone binding enforced in user_profile.schema.json and journal_entry.schema.md.

ItemId.description: snake_case id; use the canonical grep keyword from journal_entry.schema.md (cold_shower, deep_work, sleep, caffeine, meal, workout, sauna, sunlight, meditation, ...).

status.description: Free-text planning annotation on the item as generated ('done', 'unlogged', 'unlogged — analytical peak window has passed'). Descriptive only; it is NOT the completion record. Actual completion lives in log.routine.<id> and is the only thing compliance counts read.

quality.description: Subjective sleep quality 1-5 (matches the /5 convention used for graded metrics like back_pain). Mirrored as [sleep.quality] <n>.

RoutineItem.description: One routine item's outcome for the day. Absence of a key means NOT RECORDED — never infer a miss from silence; that inference is what the dual-write audit exists to prevent.

done.description: Legacy completion flag, retained so every 1.0 document stays valid. Equivalent to status: true -> 'done', false -> 'skipped' (the historical writer only ever emitted false alongside a 'SKIPPED (user-stated)' note). Prefer `status` on new writes; when both are present `status` wins.

status.description: Authoritative outcome. `done` = it happened. `skipped` = the user explicitly said they did not do it — a real, informative observation. `not_reported` = the user was asked or the item was due but no answer was given — an absence of evidence, NOT a behavior miss. Collapsing `skipped` and `not_reported` into one boolean is the defect this field exists to fix: a compliance count that treats them alike reports failures the user never had.

count.description: How many discrete units the item covered when the user gave a number but not a breakdown (e.g. supplements_breakfast count 4, 'individual items not expanded'). Keeps the quantity queryable without inventing per-item records that were never stated.

value.description: The reading (e.g. 2 for a 2/5 pain score, 58 for HRV ms).

scale.description: Optional max of a bounded scale (e.g. 5 for a /5 score). Omit for unbounded metrics.

source.description: The user's own wording for the activity, kept verbatim so the greppable description survives even when `type` is normalized to a canonical keyword.
